new_issues.title: validateFile uses parseFrontmatter, which swallows read errors, so a read failure after preflight is reported as a docType FAIL (exit 1) instead of an error, and the file is read twice.
new_issues.why: parseFrontmatter catches every error and returns found:false, and validateFile only compares data.docType, so a read failure on that first read yields a doctype failure and the later readFile catch is reachable only if the second read alone fails. But preflight has just run stat and access(R_OK) on the same file, so this needs the file to vanish or change permissions in the milliseconds between preflight and validateFile, or an EIO. The claim is true; the trigger is a narrow race, so it is hardening rather than a merge blocker.

new_issues.title: resolveTemplatePath duplicates validateFrontmatterAction's project and worktree resolution, including the 'Project not found' message.
new_issues.why: Both functions build a FileProjectStore, call resolveProjectWorktree and getById, throw the same UserError text, then call resolveOperationPath. The duplication is real and the two differ slightly (validate.ts falls back to projectPath), but both behave correctly; this is a DRY point, not a defect.

new_issues.title: SLICE_DESIGN_DOC_TYPE redefines the 'slice-design' literal that frontmatterSchema.ts still hardcodes in three places.
new_issues.why: The new constant duplicates 'slice-design' already present at frontmatterSchema.ts:74/76, 148 and 185, which do not use it. The values agree today, so behavior is correct; this is a single-source-of-truth style point.

new_issues.title: The no-files usage error throws SliceDesignValidationError rather than UserError, so it prints with an 'Error:' prefix and reports code UNKNOWN in JSON mode.
new_issues.why: handleError gives only UserError the clean message and its code; any other Error gets 'Error: ' in human mode and code UNKNOWN in JSON mode. The exit code is still 2 and the message is still printed, so the effect is cosmetic error formatting and a less specific machine code.

new_issues.title: JSON error mode is enabled only by sniffing '--json' in argv, so 'cf validate design -j' prints plain-text errors on failure.
new_issues.why: index.ts calls setJsonMode only when process.argv includes '--json' or CF_JSON=1, while withJsonOption registers '-j, --json', so the claim is true. That detection lives in index.ts and errors.ts, unchanged in base..head, and applies to every command using withJsonOption; the new command only inherits it.

new_issues.title: The new command tests never assert the JSON stderr error payload, because the harness never enables JSON error mode.
new_issues.why: The test harness registers the command on a bare Command without the entrypoint, so setJsonMode is never called and the --json exit-2 cases only check exit code and empty stdout. This is a coverage gap for paths that otherwise work through shared, pre-existing handleError code.

new_issues.title: An inline YAML comment on the docType line makes the docType comparison fail because parseFrontmatter keeps the comment in the value.
new_issues.why: parseFrontmatter takes everything after the first colon and strips only quotes, so 'docType: slice-design # note' yields 'slice-design # note' and fails the strict comparison. The claim is true, but the parser is pre-existing and shared by every frontmatter check, and project docs do not put comments on docType lines; it is an unlikely input rather than a defect introduced here.

new_issues.title: The tests read live slice documents and the guide-managed slice-design template, so ordinary doc or guide edits can break them.
new_issues.why: PASSING_DESIGNS points at four real files under project-documents/user/slices and REAL_TEMPLATE at the guide checkout, so the claim is true. It is test fragility, not wrong product behavior.
